subject: Weekly staff signal: Wins, risks, and QBR prep
messages:
From: Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.com>
To: Laura Bennett <laura_bennett@redwood.com>
Cc: Vivek Kulkarni <vivek_kulkarni@redwood.com>, Jonas Weber <jonas_weber@redwood.com>, Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>
Date: Thu, 3 May 2028 14:02:00 -0400
Subject: Weekly staff signal: Wins, risks, and QBR prep

Team — sending the weekly signal ahead of Friday's QBR dry run. Short summary below (wins / near-term risks / asks). I attached a 1-pager and raw usage snapshot for the exec pack. Please flag anything that should move into the priority slides.

WINS:
- Headroom: Dedicated pool for RetailPilot cleared certification and passed 72-hour soak; sustained 1.2M tokens/day during load tests (no SLO breaches).
- Cost optimization: Batch-kv cache change reduced median token cost by ~11% on high-concurrency routes. We'll include a results slide.
- CS: Atlas Health pilot progressed — first 3-week milestone completed; they reported a 22% latency improvement vs their self-hosted baseline.

RISKS / CONCERNS:
- Capacity tail risk: We saw two transient GPU OOMs during sequence-length spikes on p4d nodes; root cause points to an edge-case with KV eviction in an older kernel. Patch queued but current workaround is conservative batch caps which increase tail latency for a small % of requests.
- Pricing ask in negotiations: Atlas procurement is pushing for a blended rate below our floor. They want a pilot price + optional committed discount that impacts Dedicated pricing behavior.
- QBR readiness: Need one cost slide with minute-level trend for June -> Sept (Marissa, can you validate the cost breakdown by route?)

ASKS (clear, owners, due dates):
- Marissa: Validate cost-by-route dashboard and produce a 1-slide snapshot for QBR (due: 2028-05-05 EOD). Attachment: usage-snapshots.csv has the raw export.
- Jonas & Vivek: Approve proposed temporary rollback plan for batch caps if the patched kernel is delayed — decision by 2028-05-04 noon. Plan is low-risk but will increase token spend ~3-6% for 48 hours.
- Laura: Confirm whether we should include the Atlas negotiation as a redline in the QBR deck or handle offline with sales leadership.

Quick plan for Friday dry run:
- 9:00am EST: 15-min run through core slides (Jonas to lead model & infra slides)
- 9:20am EST: 10-min commercial callouts (pricing / Atlas ask)

Attachments: QBR_one-pager_v2.pdf (slide deck excerpt), usage-snapshots.csv (raw export).

Thanks — short and actionable. I can pivot slides tonight if we decide to escalate Atlas pricing.

--
Karthik Iyer
Head of Product Operations | Redwood Inference

On the Atlas negotiation: suggestion is to keep the initial QBR note as a "pilot expansion" bullet and surface the pricing ask in the commercial appendix. If leadership wants to treat it as a negotiation risk we can escalate — I won't call it a redline unless you tell me to.

Action updates:

- Jonas/Vivek: Roland from infra ran the patch in staging; if green, we schedule a canary to prod tonight (ETA 22:00 ET). If you approve the temporary rollback plan we will prepare the ops runbook entry.

Attaching the updated one-pager. Also cc'd Sofia to keep Atlas informed of the milestone progress — Sofia, thanks for the feedback this week; if procurement has immediate questions on the proposed pilot pricing, please flag and we'll set a short call.

I'll be at the dry run Friday and can talk costs — if anyone wants the raw timeseries, I left the 1-minute granularity file in the shared folder.
